answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 11% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the wharf ordering is published with the pulse batch, the canyon audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 287 account operation therefore ties up 13 million dollars of idle capital. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
